children: Patel returns to Diageo India in an expanded people leadership role covering commercial, marketing and corporate relations functions

Dharmesh Patel has been appointed Vice President – HR Business Partner, Commercial, Marketing and Corporate Relations at Diageo India, returning to the organisation after a stint as Global Finance HR Business Partner on secondment.

Patel brings more than 15 years of experience across human resources, talent management, business partnering and organisational development. His career has included senior HR roles across Diageo and other organisations, with experience spanning commercial functions, talent development, employee engagement and inclusion.

Before taking up his latest role, Patel served in a people leadership capacity at Diageo India, where his responsibilities included supporting business functions and driving talent and organisational priorities. He has also worked across HR roles with organisations including Tata Motors and other large enterprises, building experience across multiple facets of people management.

His professional profile highlights a strong focus on talent development and employee experience. Patel has also worked on learning and development and inclusion initiatives, including leading teams responsible for learning, development and inclusion and diversity. In 2014, an onboarding solution he worked on for campus recruits was recognised among the top three nationally at the People Matters Learning & Development League Awards organised by People Matters and Deloitte.

Patel holds a postgraduate qualification from Symbiosis Institute of Management Studies and has completed management and leadership programmes, including training as a Dale Carnegie Certified Trainer. He has also undertaken an Operations Consultant Course at Hamburger University.

In his new role, Patel will partner with Diageo India’s commercial, marketing and corporate relations teams on people and talent priorities. His appointment comes as the company continues to strengthen its people agenda across a workforce of more than 3,000 employees in India.
